description: Generate a runnable argparse command-line tool with a subcommand per declared name, a test module and a README. At the start of a CLI project, to get the argument plumbing and tests in place. Do not choose this when you want the subcommand logic implemented, which needs a specification. Example requests: Scaffold a CLI tool with these subcommands. | Generate an argparse entry point for my new command. | Give me a starter Python CLI with tests and a README.

accepted_price.description: The amount accepted, exactly as quoted (for example "5.00" or 5). Checked against the stored quote, so a price that moved between quote and authorize is refused rather than silently absorbed. Optional, but sent to make the acceptance explicit.

authorized_by.description: Identifier of the human or agent authorizing this job.

behaviour.description: The customer's behaviour.txt, as text. Supported: Free text. What the tool does. Maximum 1048576 bytes.

subcommands.description: The customer's subcommands.txt, as text. Supported: Plain text, one name per line. One subcommand per line. Maximum 1048576 bytes.

tool_name.description: The customer's tool_name.txt, as text. Supported: A lowercase identifier. The tool's name. Maximum 1048576 bytes.

quote_id.description: The quote_id returned by POST /v1/jobs. Required to authorize a priced capability; the service rejects a priced job that does not name the quote it issued.

name: submit_cli_tool_scaffold

access_token.description: Per-job credential. Present it as the X-Job-Token header to read the job or list it. Keep it; it is the only credential for this job.

verification.description: Independent verification. verification.ok = false means the job failed, not a partial success.

title: CLI tool scaffold
